database-systems-concepts--data-definiti.title: DDL creates the schema and its constraints
lines: FOREIGN KEY (sid) REFERENCES student(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
database-systems-concepts--data-definiti.note: DDL fixes the schema and its constraints; every later DML statement is checked against them.

database-systems-concepts--data-manipula.title: DML changes rows, not the schema
lines: UPDATE enrol SET grade = 'B' WHERE sid = 7 AND cid = 'CS301';
DELETE FROM enrol WHERE grade IS NULL;
database-systems-concepts--data-manipula.note: Each statement runs inside a transaction, so a failed third statement can leave the first two uncommitted.

database-systems-concepts--candidate-key.title: keys of student(id, email, name)
rows: any set that determines every attribute
the candidate key chosen for identity
attributes matching a key of another relation
database-systems-concepts--candidate-key.note: Minimality is what separates a candidate key from the superkeys that contain it.

database-systems-concepts--inner-join.title: inner join on a matching key
lines: JOIN   enrol   AS e ON e.sid = s.id
database-systems-concepts--inner-join.note: Only rows with a match on enrol survive, so a student with no enrolment disappears from the result.

database-systems-concepts--left-outer-jo.title: left outer join keeps unmatched rows
lines: LEFT JOIN enrol AS e ON e.sid = s.id;
database-systems-concepts--left-outer-jo.note: The unmatched left row survives with nulls on the right, which is why COUNT(e.cid) ignores it.

database-systems-concepts--null.title: three-valued AND
database-systems-concepts--null.note: NULL means unknown rather than false, so grade <> 'A' does not return rows where grade is NULL.

database-systems-concepts--view.title: a view stores the query, not the rows
lines: FROM   student s JOIN enrol e ON e.sid = s.id
SELECT name FROM cs_marks WHERE grade = 'A';
database-systems-concepts--view.note: The view is recomputed from student and enrol every time it is referenced, so it never goes stale.

database-systems-concepts--trigger.title: row-level audit trigger
lines: INSERT INTO grade_log(sid, cid, old_g, new_g)
database-systems-concepts--trigger.note: A row-level trigger fires once per changed row, inside the transaction that caused the change.

database-systems-concepts--schedule.title: an interleaved schedule S
database-systems-concepts--schedule.note: Every conflict edge runs T1 -> T2, so the precedence graph is acyclic and S is conflict-serializable, equivalent to T1 then T2.

database-systems-concepts--write-ahead-l.title: log record reaches disk before its page

steps.label: force the log record to disk
modify page X in the buffer pool
page may flush later; log is already safe
append and force the commit record c1

database-systems-concepts--write-ahead-l.note: Undo replays the old value from the log, redo the new one; the ordering rule is what makes both possible.

database-systems-concepts--two-phase-loc.title: growing then shrinking phase
database-systems-concepts--two-phase-loc.note: T1 takes every lock before releasing any, so the schedule is conflict-serializable and no cycle can form here.

database-systems-concepts--dense-index.title: dense versus sparse index
rows: scan the block after a match
the ordering key of a sorted file
database-systems-concepts--dense-index.note: A sparse index is much smaller and may fit in fewer pages, but it only works when the file is ordered by the key.
